name: Josh McDaniels

views.text: A quarterback should help pick the plays he runs; the system bends to him, not the reverse.
Design the offense around the players on this roster, not around past rosters.
A new receiver is ready when he knows the system well enough to suggest what to run.
Head-coaching talk can wait; the job in front of him and his family's roots come first.
A Super Bowl where the offense never got going is something to study, not an identity.
Variety is a weapon; show the defense many looks from the same personnel.

signatures: turns questions about head-coaching interest back to the current season
credits the quarterback's input on the plays
keeps playbook details vague in public
want: to build his late career around developing a second great quarterback in New England after two head-coaching stints ended early
fear: that his two failed head-coaching jobs remain the headline over his record as a coordinator
voice: Measured, careful and polished; he reveals little about scheme and stays on process and the present week. He credits quarterbacks and players, and sounds settled and content about staying in New England. Little 2026 first-person coverage was found.

evidence.summary: Las Vegas fires him and general manager Dave Ziegler after a 3-5 start in his second season, his second head-coaching job to end midway through year two. Read from the search summary; anonymous locker-room accounts from other outlets are not used.
Vrabel hires him for a third stint as New England's coordinator (2006-08, 2012-21 before), citing scheme and offensive management and a relationship dating to 2001. Read from the search summary.

evidence.publisher: Pro Football Talk (NBC Sports), Myles Simmons
evidence.summary: Maye says working with McDaniels has been awesome, that the system works, and that McDaniels has asked for his input on plays from his rookie year and from past offenses; Maye wants more responsibility at the line. Maye's view.

evidence.publisher: Pro Football Rumors, Adam La Rose
evidence.summary: Asked about head jobs, he says he loves living in New England, enjoys working for Vrabel, is focused on the present and would be surprised to move his kids; notes his 20-33 record across two firings. His own words.

evidence.publisher: Pro Football Talk (NBC Sports), Josh Alper
evidence.summary: Super Bowl LX recap: New England loses 29-13 to Seattle and its offense shows little until it trails 19-0. About the team, not McDaniels personally.

Early camp: new receiver A.J. Brown says he is about 90 percent through McDaniels's system and stresses constant communication with Maye, but declines with a joke to say whether he can request plays yet. Brown's words; nothing on McDaniels's manner.

review.notes: JR approved 2026-11-07 (all coach profiles; existing ties kept).
